title: Deal the folds
prompt:
Dr. Nib wants every ticket to take one turn as the validation set. Write `folds(items, k)`. It cuts `items` into `k` equal parts, in order, and returns one round per part. Each round is a pair: the part that sits out (validate) and everything else (train).

When it works, `python3 folds.py` prints three rounds, and no ticket ever appears on both sides of the same line.
expected_output:
validate ['T1', 'T2'] train ['T3', 'T4', 'T5', 'T6']
validate ['T3', 'T4'] train ['T1', 'T2', 'T5', 'T6']
validate ['T5', 'T6'] train ['T1', 'T2', 'T3', 'T4']
hints: Part number `part` starts at index `part * size` and stops just before `part * size + size`.
A slice gives the part. Two slices glued with `+` give everything before it and everything after it.
Loop `for part in range(k):`, set `start = part * size`, then `validate = items[start:start + size]` and `train = items[:start] + items[start + size:]`, and append the pair.
explain_after: In k-fold cross-validation the data is split into k parts, the model trains on k-1 of them and is checked on the last one, and the reported score is the average over the k runs [ml-049]. Your function deals the parts. scikit-learn's `cross_validate` helper does all of it, with 5 folds by default [ml-104].
